thread.title: 96-99 454 Vortec owners?
thread.first_post_html:
How many 96-2000 7400, aka, 7.4L, aka 454 owners are out there??

Seems these trucks sure have a lot of potential, but seem be awfully restricted.

I have heard exhaust really wakes these beasts up, I would like to do an x-pipe in mine and build for torque and economy. My 454 is running around 12.7-13.1 mpg so far at 55-75 mph and a mix of bumper to bumper rush hour (Dan Ryan traffic) traffic. I have 3.73's now and LT245 75 16's.

My goals are to meet the 350's mileage (so far I am very close) that my 96 Burb had, if not beat it.

What have people done to them that works or doesn't work?

I am going to work on a Wait4Me tune shortly here with agressive DFCO.
Possibly 265 75 16's to help reduce some cruise rpms (we spend a lot of time at 69-75 mph...) and ??? that might help. We live out in the boonies, so cruising at 75 ends up being the norm.... Not desired, just the norm.

I have a 98 3/4 ton with a vortec 454 in it. I have done some mods but a cam and computer tune are next. so far i have msd 6al box, blast 2 coil, taylor 8mm plug wires, tb spacer, k&n filter, baks powerpack exhaust system. runs like a top. i normally haul our race cars down the highway about 85 or so and get 14 mpg pulling 13000 lbs.

wow! I'm not alone!

I am starting to think the exhaust is the big choke. The manifolds to the muffler are very good, fat 2.25 to 2.5" dual pipes, but the muffler seems so quiet I am wondering if it is joining badly the 2 sides and causing a backpressure problem. I think true duals would be good, and an x-pipe if possible (if I can figure out how to fit it in)

You are getting better towing mileage than I get not towing. What gearing do you run? I am guessing 4.10's with the weight.

I have been pondering an custom intake plenum spacer to make for longer runners and some additional plenum area.

I'm looking at a '98 3/4 ton with the Vortec 454 right now. It's been a farm truck since it's purchase date. It has about 70k on it, and still runs strong. It was purchased to haul ammonia tanks, and has done an excellent job stock. After a simple bolt-on cat-back Flowmaster system, it did seem to pull a little better, and get a little better mileage, plus it actually had sound!

The only thing holding me back on the truck is that it's power nothing! Base model as they come 4X4. The motor is the only thing keeping me interested.

I am happy with the power at lighter throttle, but if you are on it harder, like trying to get rpms up, it doesn't have upstairs power. I need to hook a datalogger up and read what the PCM thinks is going on. I'm betting as rpms are going up, MAP (vacuum) isn't going towards zero vacuum, indicating a restriction in airflow.

The air filter to the MAF to the throttle body has some serious bends in it, but I don't think enough to kill that much power or airflow. They will be addressed shortly though. I have only a K&N on it now. I have never run it without, so I can't really tell you how much it is helping or hurting power.

If you get it for a good price, pull the drivetrain and stick into a nicer truck and swap the other drivetrain back to the farm truck and send it on its way.

That 454 should be in good shape, I can't imagine it run hard at all.

Originally Posted by N0DIH
What gearing do you run? I am guessing 4.10's with the weight.
This is the most important question here if you ask me.

I've got a '98 C3500 dually crew cab, 7.4 / 4L80E, 4.10 gears. It's got an under-the-bed wheel lift wrecker setup, 225/70/19.5 wheels/tires instead of 16's (overall a little taller than the OEM 16" setup), Ranch Hand front bumper, all power options (not a stripped down work truck), misc other accessories.. I'm not sure how much it all weighs but I guarantee you it's heavier than just about anything you can imagine that is still a "light duty" truck. I do need to scale it so I can see just how ridiculous it is.

Only mods to the drivetrain would be a pair of Flowmasters. When I stomp on it, even from a rolling start, it jumps! So do any passengers I have with me! Also got 10ish mpg on a 400 mile all highway trip, not loaded. Put on top of all this it probably hasn't been tuned up in YEARS, and I think it still needs the injector assembly upgrade.



Richard

I have 3.73's with 265-75-16 michelin atx on mine. On nice flat highway i will put it in od and keep an eye on the trans temp. never gets above 200. i have also upgraded the valve body and installed a shift kit so it wont hurt the trans to tow like this. but when hills come i will drop it back into drive. i love the bb power. you cant beat it. plus the design hasnt changed from all big blocks for years and years. just intake assembly. so if you know anything about older bb, you are good to go on thses. one GREAT thing is i can pass diesels all day running down the highway, occassionally i will catch one of them looking over at the banks powerpack sticker on the door. makes me laugh. the tune however is next. what plugs are you running? that makes a hell of a difference? so do wires?

what are your thoughts on the powerpack from Banks? Worth a lot in power? I was wondering how restrictive the muffler is.

I do want to fix up the intake tract to make it a straight shot and also keep underhood heat from getting to the filter.

Got any pictures of the parts of the Banks PP?

the Vortec big blocks run a very different injection system than the small blocks do. The bigblock injection is by far more desirable because it uses conventional fuel injectors which can be replaced with larger sizes without changing the intake manifold.

IIRC the 454 Vortec uses 24 lb/hr LT1 fuel injectors. It is rated at 290 hp and 410 lb/ft torque.

The cylinder heads are very restrictive to power production. I have seen Vortec 454's dyno at 217 hp at the rear wheels in a 1 ton truck, torque was over 320 lb ft at the wheels.

headwork along with a cam can really wake these 454's up. They are a step up from the TBI 454's which make their peak torque at 1800 rpm. They came in 230 hp 385 lb/ft and 255hp 405 lb/ft flavours.

A nice set of aluminum 502 heads woiuld work nicely in tehse trucks, or drop in 502 shortblock.

peace
pauly

I have seen a lot of people say the L29 heads (96-02 454) are some of the best kept secrets of GM, similar comments that they said on the L31 heads.

Head flow #'s I have seen haven't been bad like the L19 and L03/L05 heads. Cam is a little small, 204/209ish. Most people on TeamChevelle.com said a cam swap makes this engine a monster. The ZZ502 cam being one very popular.

Even the HT502 uses the exact same heads and cam making 338 hp and 510-520 lb/ft torque.

Being I haven't seen a "head to head" comparisson on these engines I can't really say if the real reason these 454's are dogs compared to what they should be.

Honestly, the #1 reason I wanted the 454 over the 350 was the injectors. I can't run E85 in a 350 at all without an intake swap. The 454, easy. A set of 44# injectors on stock PCM tune and you are set for E85. Add some additional timing and you should have it running pretty good. BUT, you are still single fuel. Can't swap back and forth....

There was someone who got a wait4me tune with a 5 speed 454 and ran a dyno run, I can't seem to find the post, anyone have any ideas how to do a better search?? I don't remember if it was the tech or perf forum.

Vortec 454 heads are small ovals not peanut ports hence the "best kept secret". They pick up flow very well with minor porting and flow better then peanuts while still keeping the ports small for great torque.

Put me on the list.
She is still running.
Just bought one today, the one in my signature so I am enjoying reading all the posts on here about the 454 equipped trucks, I am ready to start buying HP goodies lol.

I bought one two weeks ago. A 98 reg cab 3500 4x4 with the 454. It has 95,000 miles on it and runs strong. I don't know what my mileage is yet. Fuel gauge also acts a little funny. Its still all stock. I'll probably do the exhaust sometime in the future.

Wayne
What tune would you gentlemen suggest to get just a shade bit more power out of the BB?

I have a Wait4Me tune. Overall good. It REALLY wakes up with 93 octane. I think he is still pretty conservative with 87 octane. But still a world difference over stock. I suspect WOT power is similar on 87 octane, but much improved in the midrange and 93 octane (there is 2 octane maps, so it can react with both if the octane is pumped up)

Best $75 you will spend.

NOTE: Jesse pulls the latest tune from GM, and in my case and others with 454's, got the "Towing Improvement Program" which changes it to permanent Tow/Haul mode. You don't get lock up on the converter till 68-69 mph with 3.73's. GREAT when towing, but without, not ideal for mpg. You have to get up to 70 mphish to get "best" economy. It won't hurt, just mpg. Trans could care less. TCC lockup and unlock while towing is a setup for disaster. TCC's aren't designed for that much abuse for lots of towing. So I left mine as is.

If you can stomach 93 octane, get a 93 octane tune, or maybe a 90-93 octane tune. The performance is dramatic. If you have a Wait4Me tune, and haven't filled up with 93, go to some 0-60 times and then fill up with 93 (try to keep vehicle weight similar and octane pure as you can) and you will see some improvments. It will put the smile back on your face!

Excellent, thats what I needed to know. I want him to possibly try and keep the converter locked up until 3/4 to full throttle for the simple fact that with the stuff I have done to the truck it actually has more torque around 1800 rather than 3000 when the converter unlocks. How long does it take for Jesse to get a tune, I am just going to order the whole computer. How do I get ahold of him.

I got my wait4me tune for my 454 awhile ago but it has been great so far. for whatever reason my converter locks at about 75-76 mph instead of 69-70 and rpm's drop by about 100 and i have 3.73's. overall it was a good improvement, in addition to my other mods i really feel that my truck is now way faster even with heavy 20 inch rims than it was stock with 16's and 245/75/16's. it was kind of a dog off the line and would barely chirp the little tires, but now i mash it and it roasts the bigger tires until i let off the gas and it kicks down really hard and flies. i would love to have some port work done and a cam swap though...

I have a bone stock 98 K3500 CCLB. 454/4L80E/4:10 gears. The stock injectors where leaking at around 108K miles, so I replaced with Bosch. Better design, but the same rating (19lb/hr). It came with the factory HD air cleaner (great big round sucker) and true dual exhaust. Right now it has glass packs, but that's gonna change soon.
I've never run it down the road empty, seems I'm always hauling something. Last big run was crammed full in the bed and towing a car hauler with minivan, about 14K lbs all told. I got 10-11 the whole trip. Around town I get the same. Lately it's been hesitating a bit, so I think it's time for new ignition parts. My truck doesn't feel restricted at all, when I step on it the truck just jumps. No problem roasting tires if I'm not careful. At this point I don't really plan any big upgrades other than ignition. Bankspowered98 has pretty much what I'll be going to.

rewrite.rewritten_title: 454 Vortec Owners Unite: Experiences and Advice
rewrite.summary: This thread discusses the experiences of owners with General Motors' 96-99 7.4L (Vortec 454) engines, focusing on their potential, modifications, and performance.
seo_outline: Popular Modifications for Power and Economy
Experiences with Tuning and Exhaust Systems
rewrite.rewritten_article_markdown:
This thread discusses the experiences of owners with General Motors' 96-99 7.4L (Vortec 454) engines, focusing on their potential, modifications, and performance.

General Motors introduced the Vortec 454 in the late 1990s as a powerful alternative to smaller V8 engines. However, many owners have noted that these engines are often restricted by various components such as the intake manifold and exhaust system (Post ID: 2657).

Several mods have been popular among owners. These include performance exhaust systems like Banks Powerpack or Flowmaster setups (Post ID: 2661). Some enthusiasts also recommend a cam swap, especially using a ZZ502 camshaft (Post ID: 2664), to unlock more potential from the engine.

Tuning plays a crucial role in enhancing performance. A Wait4Me tune has been widely recommended as it significantly improves midrange and WOT power (Post ID: 2671). However, some owners noted that stock PCM tunes can also provide decent performance, especially with higher octane fuel (Post ID: 3098).

Owners have shared their experiences regarding towing efficiency. Those who tow often find that 454-equipped trucks can offer better performance when tuned properly for towing applications (Post ID: 2670).

post_rewrites.rewritten_content:
How many owners of 1996-2000 Chevrolet 7400 trucks, with a 7.4L or 454 engine, are out there? These trucks have great potential but seem limited. I've heard that exhaust modifications can significantly improve performance. My truck currently averages around 12.7 to 13.1 mpg on highways between 55 and 75 mph, including heavy traffic.

I'm planning an x-pipe installation and a torque-focused build for better economy. My current setup includes 3.73 gears and LT245 75/16 tires. My goal is to match or exceed the fuel efficiency of my previous 1996 model, which averaged around 350 mpg. I plan to install a Wait4Me tune with aggressive DFCO settings soon. Additionally, I may switch to 265/75/16 tires to reduce cruise RPMs, as we frequently drive between 69 and 75 mph.

Living in the countryside means most of our driving is at these higher speeds, which isn't ideal but has become a norm.

I have a 98 model truck with a Vortec 454 engine. I've made several modifications, including an MSD 6AL ignition box, Blast 2 coils, Taylor 8mm spark plugs, a tubular bumper spacer, a K&N air filter, and the BACS PowerPack exhaust system. The truck runs well, and I typically haul race cars at around 85 mph on the highway while pulling 13,000 pounds and achieving about 14 mpg.

I'm glad I'm not alone in thinking the exhaust might be the issue. The manifolds to the muffler are well-designed, featuring 2.25 to 2.5-inch dual pipes, but the muffler's quiet operation makes me suspect a potential backpressure problem due to poor joining of the two sides.

I believe true dual exhaust and an X-pipe would improve performance if feasible. You're getting better towing mileage than I am without towing; what gearing are you using? Given your weight, I'm guessing 4.10 gears. I've been considering a custom intake plenum spacer to lengthen the runners and increase plenum volume.

I'm considering a 1998 3/4-ton truck with a Vortec 454 engine. Purchased primarily for hauling ammonia tanks, it has been used exclusively as a farm truck and now shows around 70,000 miles. It still performs well. After installing a simple bolt-on Flowmaster cat-back exhaust system, there was noticeable improvement in performance and fuel efficiency, along with improved sound quality. The main drawback is its lack of power for modern standards. The engine remains the primary reason I am interested in this truck.

I am satisfied with the engine's performance at lighter throttle but notice a lack of power when trying to increase RPMs. I plan to use a datalogger to analyze the Powertrain Control Module (PCM) data and identify any issues.

The problem likely stems from restricted airflow, indicated by the Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) not reaching zero vacuum as RPMs increase. The air filter to the Mass Air Flow (MAF) sensor to the throttle body has several bends, but I do not believe they are significant enough to cause substantial power loss.

I currently have a K&N filter installed and have never run without it, so its impact on performance is unknown. If you purchase it at a good price, consider swapping drivetrains between trucks for a more refined setup.

The 454 cubic inch engine appears to be in good condition and has not been subjected to heavy use.

I run 4.10 gears with the weight in my '98 C3500 dually crew cab equipped with a 7.4L/4L80E transmission. It has an under-the-bed wheel lift wrecker setup, 225/70/19.5 tires (taller than the original 16-inch setup), a Ranch Hand front bumper, and all power options. The truck is heavily accessorized but likely weighs more than most light-duty trucks. I need to scale it to see its weight accurately. Only drivetrain modifications include Flowmasters. Even from a rolling start, stomping on the gas causes significant acceleration, including for passengers. It averages about 10 mpg on a 400-mile highway trip when not heavily loaded. The truck has likely not been tuned up in years and may need an injector assembly upgrade.

I have 3.73 gears with 265/75R16 Michelin ATX tires. On flat highways, I run in overdrive and monitor the transmission temperature; it never exceeds 200°F. I've also upgraded the valve body and installed a shift kit to ensure my transmission can handle towing. When encountering hills, I switch back to drive.

I appreciate the low-end torque and love how this setup mirrors older big-block designs, with only minor changes in the intake assembly. If you're familiar with old big-blocks, you’ll be well-prepared for these.

One great advantage is the ability to easily pass diesel trucks on the highway. Occasionally, I catch them looking at my powerpack sticker, which makes me smile.

The next step is tuning the ECU. What spark plugs and wires are you using? They significantly impact performance.

What are your thoughts on the Banks PowerPack? It's powerful, but I'm curious about its muffler restriction. I plan to modify the intake for better airflow and protect the filter from underhood heat. Do you have any pictures of the relevant parts?

Originally posted by bankspowered98:
I run 3.73 gears with 265/75R16 Michelin ATX tires. On flat highways, I shift into overdrive and monitor transmission temp; it rarely exceeds 200°F. I've also upgraded the valve body and installed a shift kit to prevent damage from towing. However, on hills, I revert to drive. The power is impressive, and the design hasn't changed much since big-blocks were introduced. Familiarity with older big-blocks makes these easy to work with. One great advantage is passing diesel trucks easily on the highway. The tuning is next; what plugs are you using? And do wires make a significant difference?

I believe this is the most critical question here. I own a 1998 Chevrolet C3500 dually crew cab with a 7.4L/4L80E transmission and 4.10 gears. It features an under-the-bed wheel lift wrecker setup, 225/70/19.5 wheels/tires (taller than the original 16-inch setup), a Ranch Hand front bumper, all power options, and various accessories. The truck is significantly heavier than typical light-duty models due to these modifications.

For weight considerations, I need to perform scaling tests. The only drivetrain modification includes Flowmaster exhausts. Despite this, even moderate acceleration can cause noticeable jumps in the truck and any passengers. On a 400-mile highway trip with no load, it achieved approximately 10 miles per gallon.

The vehicle hasn't been maintained recently and likely needs an injector upgrade as the Vortec big block injection system is more flexible for power increases. The 454 Vortec runs on 24 lb/hr LT1 fuel injectors and can produce up to 290 horsepower and 410 pound-feet of torque. Restrictive cylinder heads limit its power output, but headwork and a camshaft could significantly enhance performance. TBI 454s typically generate peak torque at 1800 RPM with ratings of either 385 lb/ft or 405 lb/ft. Replacing the heads with aluminum 502 heads or using a 502 shortblock would be beneficial.

I've heard that the L29 heads (96-02 454) are among GM's best-kept secrets, similar to the L31 heads. While flow numbers aren't impressive like those of the L19 or L03/L05 heads, they're still decent. The cam is slightly small at about 204/209. Many on TeamChevelle.com suggest a cam swap can significantly enhance performance, with popular choices including the ZZ502 and HT502, which produce around 338 hp and 510-520 lb-ft of torque.

I haven't conducted a "head-to-head" comparison, so I can't definitively say why these 454 engines are often considered underperforming. However, the primary reason I opted for the 454 over the 350 was its compatibility with E85 fuel. Unlike the 350, which requires an intake swap to run E85, the 454 can use stock PCM tuning with a set of 44# injectors. Additional timing adjustments can further optimize performance, though it remains single-fuel-only.

I recall seeing a post about someone who installed a wait4me tune with a 5-speed 454 and performed a dyno run. I can’t find the post now. Does anyone know how to refine my search? It’s unclear whether it was posted in the tech or performance forum.

Vortec 454 heads feature small oval ports, not peanut ports, which makes them a "best kept secret." These heads excel in flow improvement with minimal porting and outperform peanut ports while maintaining small port size for excellent torque.
Add me to the list. She is still active.
I recently purchased one of these trucks and am eager to read through the discussions about the 454-equipped models. I'm excited to begin acquiring high-performance parts.
I purchased a 1998注册的四驱卡車，搭载3500车型和454发动机。行驶里程为95,000英里，运行状况良好。我的实际里程还在统计中。油量表偶尔会显示异常。目前车辆仍保持原厂状态。我计划将来更换排气系统。 Wayne
What tuning suggestions do you have for increasing power output in the BB?

The Wait4Me tune performs well overall, significantly boosting performance with 93 octane fuel. While it remains conservative with 87 octane, there is a noticeable improvement over stock settings. The power delivery is similar on 87 octane but notably enhanced in the midrange and at higher octane levels.

This tuning is highly recommended for those willing to spend $75, as it provides substantial performance gains. Jesse recently updated his tune with the "Towing Improvement Program," enabling permanent Tow/Haul mode. The transmission does not engage lock-up until around 68-69 mph with a 3.73 ratio, which is ideal for towing but may not be optimal for fuel efficiency.

To maximize economy, you need to reach approximately 70 mph for the best results, though this won't harm your vehicle. However, TCC lockup and unlock during towing can lead to potential issues due to excessive abuse, so I keep my setup as is.

For those who can use 93 octane fuel, consider getting a 93 octane tune or a range between 90-93 octane for even more dramatic improvements. If you already have the Wait4Me tune and haven't used 93 octane, try comparing 0-60 times before and after filling up with 93 octane to see the difference in performance.

That's helpful information. I want to keep the converter locked up until around 3/4 to full throttle because my modifications have increased torque closer to 1800 RPM rather than 3000 when the converter unlocks. Approximately how long will it take Jesse to create a tune? Should I order the entire computer system instead? How can I contact Jesse?

I recently installed my wait4me tune for my 454 cubic inch engine, and while it has significantly improved performance, the converter locks around 75-76 mph instead of the intended 69-70 mph. This results in an RPM drop of about 100 with a 3.73 gear ratio. Despite this issue, overall, the improvement is substantial. My truck now feels much faster than it was stock, even with heavy 20-inch rims compared to the original 16-inch ones. Before the tune, it struggled off the line and barely chirped the small tires; now, flooring the accelerator roasts the larger tires until I lift off the gas, causing a hard downshift and rapid acceleration.

I would like to consider port work and a cam swap in the future to further enhance performance.

I own a 1998 K3500 CCLB with 454/4L80E/4:10 gears. The original injectors leaked around 108,000 miles and were replaced with Bosch units, which have the same 19 lb/hr rating but a better design. It comes equipped with the factory HD air cleaner and true dual exhaust; I plan to install glass packs soon. The truck is rarely driven empty, often carrying various loads. A recent haul involved a bed full of cargo and towing a car hauler weighing about 14,000 pounds, yielding 10-11 mpg throughout the trip. City driving also averages similar fuel efficiency. Lately, there has been some hesitation, leading me to consider new ignition parts. The truck feels unrestricted; stepping on the gas causes immediate acceleration, and it can easily overrev if not careful. No major upgrades are planned beyond the ignition system, which will likely follow Bankspowered98's setup.
